- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns positive — forecast lags 1–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, assuming price will return to historical mean too quickly — fails to account for structural volatility.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to short-term sentiment, leading to overfitting to recent sentiment peaks — ignore sentiment if it’s not persistent.
- When sentiment is rising but price is flat, model tends to overreact — forecast jumps too early, missing consolidation phase.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment can reverse quickly, especially in volatile markets.
